items.followUp: State one living and one non-living characteristic of viruses.

rubric.why: Viruses are inactive outside a living host.
rubric.description: States that viruses are inert or inactive outside a living host.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying their inactive state outside the host.

rubric.why: Viruses show a living characteristic by reproducing inside a host.
rubric.description: States that viruses reproduce or multiply inside a living host cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying reproduction inside the host.

modelAnswer: Outside a living host, viruses are inert and do not carry out life activities.
Inside a living host cell, they reproduce and show living characteristics.

items.followUp: Write any two principles of the cell theory.

rubric.why: This states that cells make up living organisms.
rubric.description: States that all living organisms are composed of one or more cells.

rubric.why: Either statement gives a distinct principle of cell theory.
rubric.description: States that the cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life, or that new cells arise from pre-existing cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid principle distinct from the first principle.

modelAnswer: All living organisms are composed of one or more cells.
The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life.

items.followUp: Differentiate between active transport and facilitated diffusion.

rubric.why: Diffusion moves particles down their concentration gradient.
rubric.description: States that diffusion is the movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the direction of movement in diffusion.

rubric.why: Osmosis specifically involves water moving through a selectively permeable membrane.
rubric.description: States that osmosis is the movement of water through a selectively permeable membrane from a dilute solution towards a more concentrated solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying water, the membrane, and the direction of movement in osmosis.

modelAnswer: Diffusion is the movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration; it can occur in gases and liquids.
Osmosis is the movement of water through a selectively permeable membrane from a dilute solution towards a more concentrated solution.

items.followUp: What happens to a cell during apoptosis?

rubric.why: Apoptotic bodies form as small membrane-bound fragments during programmed cell death.
rubric.description: Identifies apoptotic bodies as small membrane-bound fragments or vesicles formed from a cell undergoing apoptosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing their formation and structure.

rubric.why: Apoptotic bodies are removed by being engulfed by other cells.
rubric.description: States that apoptotic bodies are engulfed by phagocytes or neighbouring cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing their removal.

modelAnswer: During apoptosis, the cell breaks into small membrane bound fragments called apoptotic bodies.
These bodies are engulfed by neighbouring cells or phagocytes.
